attachments.title: Source clinical note
attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-04-15
Provider: Dr. James Chen, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Severe pain and vision loss in right eye after power saw accident at construction job site

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This 35-year-old male with prior finger rash and fever presents to the ED. He reports that something struck his eye while he was using a power saw.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Herpetic whitlow or viral lymphangitis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Repair of open globe injury, right eye
- Wisdom teeth extraction

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: Hypertension
- Mother: Hypothyroidism
- Paternal grandfather: Type 2 diabetes

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Social, 1-2 drinks per week. Occupation: Self-employed landscape contractor; former construction worker and dental assistant.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, his right eye appears deformed with a teardrop-shaped pupil and there is a shallow anterior chamber compared to the left eye. Visual acuity is significantly reduced in the affected eye. The patient is unable to see the number of fingers presented in front of the right eye, whereas the left eye has a visual acuity of 20/20. An afferent pupillary defect is noted in the right eye. Intraocular pressure is 8 mmHg in the right eye and 14 mmHg in the left eye. Fluorescein staining shows a positive Seidel test. No other injuries are noted.

attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-10-15
Provider: Dr. Raj Patel, MD
Department: Dermatology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Itchy, slowly expanding annular rash on left forearm present for 2 weeks

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns to Dermatology with a new concern, having presented previously in January for a painful finger rash and in April for an occupational eye injury. He reports that the rash began as a small red spot and has gradually expanded outward. He denies any recent travel, new medications, or known allergies.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Herpetic whitlow or viral lymphangitis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Open globe laceration (diagnosed 2020-04-15)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Repair of open globe injury, right eye
- Wisdom teeth extraction

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: Hypertension
- Mother: Hypothyroidism
- Paternal grandfather: Type 2 diabetes

SOCIAL HISTORY:
He works as a gardener and often comes into contact with various plants and soil.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, there is a well-demarcated, erythematous, annular plaque with a raised border and central clearing on his left forearm. There are no vesicles or pustules, and the rest of the skin examination is unremarkable.

OTHER STUDIES:
A potassium hydroxide (KOH) examination of skin scrapings from the affected area reveals branching hyphae.
